summary: The prepared base already excluded width-dependent EAGLE draft-extend select_index buffers from the process-wide pool, directly preventing cross-width aliasing that can turn a valid wide index into a narrow-graph gather OOB. The change makes that invariant intrinsic to EagleDraftExtendInputBuffers and adds a failing-before/passing-after narrow-versus-wide regression.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-c4bad979ad90/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_buffer_registry.py -k eagle_width_specific_select_index (with the specialized exclusion temporarily disabled)
tests.what_was_measured: The regression observed identical select_index data pointers for narrow and wide EAGLE capture widths, proving the pre-fix aliasing mechanism.
46 unit tests passed, including independent narrow [1,3] over four rows and wide [3,7] over eight rows, plus draft-extend selected-row logits behavior.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-c4bad979ad90/raw/gpu-gather-check.log and gpu-health-after-boundary.log identify AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 and record exact numerical output. This was a kernel-level fixture, not the reported serving workload.
remaining_limitations: No Tesla V100 or CUDA environment was assigned; the CUDA device-assert, NCCL abort, and Xid 43 signatures were not reproduced.
Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned, so the reported TP=4 PCIe-only distributed workload was not run.
RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 weights and the V100-specific image/backends were unavailable.

The deterministic evidence verifies the candidate cross-width gather-index mechanism and its regression, but does not establish that it is the sole root cause of the original concurrent constrained-tool serving crash.
